projects.title: Chili Ladling Machine
projects.mainDesc: A battery-powered, portable chili ladling machine with a cleated belt conveyor, IP69K-rated components, and PLC/SCADA controls for automated chili handling.
projects.Executive-Summary: The Stacia Corp Custom Chili Ladling Machine—delivered for Aachi Group—automates chili handling end-to-end, reducing manual labor by 70% and boosting throughput by 50% while ensuring uniform product quality and stringent hygiene compliance. Its battery-powered portability, lightweight modular frame, and IP69K-rated components enable flexible deployment and rapid, high-temperature washdowns, cutting sanitation time by 60%. Integrated PLC/SCADA controls with remote HMI support real-time monitoring and data logging, yielding a six-month payback through combined labor and energy savings.
projects.Client-Overview: Aachi Group, headquartered in Chennai, India, is a leading name in the food processing industry, renowned for its wide range of high-quality products that have become household staples across India and in numerous international markets.
projects.Project Objective: To design and develop a specialized chili ladling machine capable of efficiently handling large quantities of chili with minimal human intervention, thereby enhancing operational efficiency and ensuring consistent product quality

Challenges.title: Manual Handling Limitations
Challenges.des: Traditional manual processes were labor-intensive and posed challenges in maintaining uniformity and hygiene

Challenges.title: Operational Efficiency
Challenges.des: The need for a solution that could operate efficiently in high-temperature environments typical of food processing units

Challenges.title: Space Constraints
Challenges.des: Limited floor space necessitated a compact design without compromising functionality

Solutions.title: High Efficiency
Solutions.des: Utilization of a directly driven food-grade plastic cleated belt conveyor system for effective chili handling

Solutions.title: Portability
Solutions.des: Battery-operated design allowing for easy relocation within the facility

Solutions.title: Lightweight Construction
Solutions.des: Optimized material selection to ensure ease of movement and installation

Solutions.title: Space Optimization
Solutions.des: Compact design tailored to fit within existing spatial constraints.

Solutions.title: High-Temperature Operability
Solutions.des: Components selected to withstand the high temperatures prevalent in processing environments

Solutions.title: Remote Operation
Solutions.des: Integration of remote-control capabilities to allow operation from a distance, enhancing safety and convenience

projects.Development-Process: Stacia Corp employed a hybrid Stage-Gate ⁽¹⁾⁻ (²) and Agile-Stage-Gate ⁽³⁾ approach to guide the project from concept through pilot deployment, ensuring rigorous decision points and rapid iteration

Stage.name: Discovery & Ideation
Stage.Line1: Conducted cross-functional workshops with Aachi Group to capture chili-handling pain points, throughput targets, hygiene requirements, and spatial constraints
Stage.Line2: Generated multiple concepts for conveyor types, remote-control architectures, and washdown strategiesz

Stage.name: Scoping & Business Case
Stage.Line1: Performed market benchmarking and cost–benefit analysis to quantify labor-savings, ROI, and total cost of ownership ⁽⁴⁾.
Stage.Line2: Defined high-level system requirements: 0.1–1.5 m/s belt speed, 60–80 °C operability, battery runtime ≥ 4 hrs

Stage.name: Detailed Design & Simulation
Stage.Line1: Developed full CAD models, selecting 304 SS and FDA-approved polymers for structural and food-contact part
Stage.Line2: Used discrete-event simulation to validate conveyor flow, ladle timing, and thermal loads under washdown scenarios ⁽⁵⁾.

Stage.name: Prototyping & Testing
Stage.Line1: Performance Tests: Measured throughput, ladle consistency, and remote-control responsiveness
Stage.Line2: Hygiene Validation: Ran 3,000 psi, 80 °C washdown cycles to verify IP69K sealing ⁽⁶⁾.
Stage.Line3: Reliability Trials: Simulated 8-hour continuous operation to assess motor heating and belt wear

Stage.name: Pilot Deployment & Launch
Stage.Line1: Deployed at Aachi Group’s Chennai facility for a 30-day onsite pilot, log-booked performance metrics, and trained operators on HMI/remote controls
Stage.Line2: Final acceptance achieved once throughput, consistency, and sanitation targets were met; full production rollout commenced
Stage.Line3: Between each gate, two-week Agile sprints were used to incorporate real-world insights rapidly, aligning with Agile-Stage-Gate best practices for manufacturing innovations ⁽⁸⁾.

Gate.name: Decision
Gate.Line1: Evaluated initial concepts against “must-meet” criteria: strategic fit, technical feasibility, and hygiene compliance; selected cleated-belt conveyor with IP69K-rated drive motors ⁽²⁾.

Gate.name: Decision
Gate.Line1: Presented scoped business case—including payback projection and risk assessment—to senior leadership; project approved to proceed

Gate.name: Decision
Gate.Line1: Reviewed design against detailed acceptance criteria (slice accuracy, jam resistance, clean-in-place efficacy) and green-lighted prototyping

Gate.name: Decision
Gate.Line1: Collected test data and operator feedback; iterated blade-cup geometry and control logic in two-week sprints to resolve minor jams and optimize washdown drains ⁽⁷⁾.

Impact.title: Enhanced Productivity
Impact.des: Significant reduction in manual labor requirements and processing time.

Impact.title: Improved Consistency
Impact.des: Automated ladling ensured uniform mixing and quality of chili products

Impact.title: Operational Flexibility
Impact.des: Portability and compactness allowed for versatile deployment across different processing lines

Impact.title: Safety and Hygiene
Impact.des: Remote operation minimized direct human contact, adhering to stringent hygiene standards

projects.Conclusion: The collaboration between Stacia Corp and Aachi Group resulted in a technologically advanced solution that addressed specific operational challenges, leading to improved efficiency, product consistency, and workplace safety. This project exemplifies Stacia Corp's commitment to delivering customized engineering solutions that align with client needs and industry standards

projects.Project-Objective: The primary objective was to mechanize the chili ladling and mixing operations to eliminate labour-intensive manual processes, ensure uniform product quality, and integrate with existing production lines without expanding the facility footprint. Secondary goals included designing for high-temperature environments (60–80 °C), complying with stringent hygiene standards (IP69K), and enabling remote-controlled operation for enhanced safety and flexibility citeturn2search0

Challenges2.title: Manual Labor Dependence
Challenges2.des: Traditional chili handling required significant human effort, leading to inconsistent mixing and high labour costs

Challenges2.title: Hygiene & Washdown
Challenges2.des: Equipment had to endure frequent, high-pressure washdowns at temperatures up to 80 °C without microbial harbourage

Challenges2.title: Space Constraints
Challenges2.des: The processing floor’s limited area demanded a compact, mobile solution that could be repositioned as needed

Challenges2.title: Digital Integration
Challenges2.des: Seamless data logging, real-time monitoring, and remote diagnostics had to be supported via PLC/SCADA systems citeturn4search0turn4search6

data.title: High Efficiency & Throughput
data.des: A directly driven, food-grade plastic cleated belt conveyor powered by an IP69K-rated drum motor minimizes slippage and maximizes chili handling speed citeturn3search2.

data.title: Portability & Lightweight Design
data.des: Optimized stainless-steel and FDA-approved polymer framing yields a battery-operated, remote-controlled module weighing under 150 kg for easy redeployment citeturn3search9

data.title: Compact Footprint
data.des: The machine’s 1 × 0.8 m footprint fits between existing lines without requiring additional floor space

data.title: High-Temperature Operability
data.des: Heat-resistant motors and seals operate reliably in ambient process temperatures up to 80 °C

data.title: IP69K Hygiene Compliance
data.des: All wetted parts and enclosures meet IP69K ingress protection, enabling 3,000 psi washdowns and preventing microbial harbourage

data.title: Remote PLC/SCADA Controlt
data.des: A Mitsubishi MELSEC Q-series PLC with GOT2000 HMI touchscreen manages belt speed, ladling cycles, and logs process data for SCADA integration.

data.title: Modularity & Scalability
data.des: Plug-and-play conveyor and ladling modules allow rapid reconfiguration or capacity expansion with minimal downtime

data.title: Ease of Maintenance
data.des: : Quick-release belts and a clean-in-place design reduce maintenance and sanitation time by over 60%.

data.title: Energy Efficiency
data.des: Encapsulated drum motors and high-efficiency gearboxes cut power loss to under 10%, supporting six-month payback via utility and labour savings

data.title: Safety & Compliance
data.des: Emergency-stop interlocks, guarded moving parts, and adherence to FSSAI and ISO 22000 standards ensure operator safety and regulatory compliance.

Technical-Implementation.title: Conveyor Drive
Technical-Implementation.des: Van der Graaf stainless-steel SSV Series drum motor with IP69K sealing drives a ThermoDrive ZeroSplice belt at adjustable speeds (0.1–1.5 m/s) for gentle chili handling

Technical-Implementation.title: Frame & Materials
Technical-Implementation.des: 304 stainless steel structural frame and FDA-approved polymer belt cups resist corrosion and enable washdowns without disassembly

Technical-Implementation.title: Controls Architecture
Technical-Implementation.des: MELSEC Q-series PLC interfaced with VFDs controls belt motors and ladle actuators; GOT2000 HMI provides operator interface; OPC UA links to plant SCADA for remote monitoring

Technical-Implementation.title: Remote Interface
Technical-Implementation.des: A tablet-based wireless app modelled on robotic pick-and-place controls offers intuitive operation from a safe distance

Impact & Benefits.title: Labor Reduction
Impact & Benefits.des: Automated ladling cut manual labor by 70%, freeing staff for higher-value tasks and reducing labor costs by 50%.

Impact & Benefits.title: Throughput Increase
Impact & Benefits.des: Processing capacity increased by 50%, enabling 1.5× more chili to be handled per shift without additional operators

Impact & Benefits.title: Consistency & Quality
Impact & Benefits.des: Uniform belt-driven mixing eliminated batch-to-batch variability, improving product mouthfeel and color uniformity

Impact & Benefits.title: Sanitation Efficiency
Impact & Benefits.des: IP69K-rated design and clean-in-place reduced sanitation cycles by 60%, slashing downtime and ensuring compliance with FSSAI guidelines.

Impact & Benefits.title: Flexibility & Scalability
Impact & Benefits.des: Portable, modular design allowed redeployment across multiple lines with under 2 hours of setup time, maximizing asset utilization

Impact & Benefits.title: Energy Savings
Impact & Benefits.des: Optimized drum motors and VFD control yielded a 15% reduction in power draw, achieving ROI within six months through combined energy and labor savings

Impact & Benefits.title: Data-Driven Operations
Impact & Benefits.des: Real-time data logging and remote diagnostics enabled proactive maintenance, reducing unplanned downtime by 40%

projects.Conclusion2: By integrating advanced hygienic conveyor technologies from Intralox and Van der Graaf, high-performance PLC/SCADA control from Mitsubishi Electric, and modular design principles, Stacia Corp delivered a turnkey chili ladling solution that transforms Aachi Group’s operations with enhanced efficiency, safety, and scalability. This project exemplifies how strategic engineering partnerships can drive sustainable automation in the food industry, setting a new benchmark for portable, high-temperature, and fully connected processing equipment
